say.en: A bank lets another firm run its call centre, a burger chain opens 300 outlets owned by local investors, and a mobile company sells in 40 countries. These are three of the biggest trends in modern business. In this lesson: Explain outsourcing BPO and KPO, its merits and limits.
Explain franchising and its merits.
Describe the features of multinational corporations.

body.en: *Outsourcing* is contracting out a business activity, usually a non-core one, to an outside specialist. Business process outsourcing (BPO) covers routine services such as call centres, payroll and data entry; knowledge process outsourcing (KPO) covers expert work such as research, analytics, legal and medical services. It lets a firm focus on its core work, use specialists' skills and economies of scale, and turn fixed costs into variable ones. Its limits include loss of control, risk to confidential data, dependence on the vendor and resistance from employees.

points.en: Contract out non-core work to specialists
BPO: routine processes; KPO: knowledge work

body.en: *Franchising* is an arrangement in which the franchisor gives the franchisee the right to use its brand, products and methods in return for fees and royalties, while the franchisee invests in and runs the outlet. It lets the brand expand quickly with others' capital, and gives the franchisee a proven business model. A multinational corporation (MNC) has its headquarters in one country and operations in many. MNCs have huge resources, advanced technology, product innovation, global marketing and centralised control. They bring capital, technology and jobs to host countries, but may also crowd out local firms and send profits home.

points.en: Franchisor: brand, system, training; franchisee: capital, management, fees
MNC: one headquarters, operations in many countries
MNC features: resources, technology, global brands, centralised control

problem.en: A company handles 1,25,000 support calls a year. Its own centre would cost ₹40 lakh a year plus ₹20 a call; a BPO charges ₹45 a call. Which is cheaper, and at what volume would the answer change?

steps.en: Break-even: 40,00,000/(45 − 20) = 1,60,000 calls; above this, in-house is cheaper.

answer.en: Outsource now (saves ₹8.75 lakh); above 1,60,000 calls an own centre becomes cheaper.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. A company handles 1,25,000 support calls a year. Its own centre would cost ₹40 lakh a year plus ₹20 a call; a BPO charges ₹45 a call. Which is cheaper, and at what volume would the answer change?

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. A company handles 1,25,000 support calls a year. Its own centre would cost 40 rupees lakh a year plus 20 rupees a call; a BPO charges 45 rupees a call. Which is cheaper, and at what volume would the answer change?
In-house: 40,00,000 plus 1,25,000 times 20 equals 65,00,000 rupees.
Outsourced: 1,25,000 times 45 equals 56,25,000 rupees.
Outsourcing is cheaper by 8,75,000 rupees.
Break-even: 40,00,000 over 45 minus 20 equals 1,60,000 calls; above this, in-house is cheaper.
So the answer is Outsource now saves 8.75 rupees lakh; above 1,60,000 calls an own centre becomes cheaper.
